question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both sides of the equation by $2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot {3}^{x} & =54 \\ \frac{2\cdot {3}^{x}}{2} & =\frac{54}{2} \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot {3}^{x}}{\cancel{2}} & =27 \\ {3}^{x} & =27\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite $27$ as $3^3$ so that both sides have the same base:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x}={3}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the exponents, we get ${\color{blue}x}={\color{blue}3}.$
